item.title: The chromatin context differently impacts prime editors and base editors and controls the fidelity and purity of base editing.
item.abstract: Base editors and prime editors allow changing specific genomic sequences without chromosomal breakage. However, the role of the chromatin environment and its underlying factors on the efficiency, product fidelity, and purity of prime editing versus base editing is unknown. Here, using human cellular systems that monitor the efficiency and fidelity of gene-editing tools at isogenic target sites controlled by specific epigenetic remodeling factors, we report that heterochromatin impinged by the Krüppel-associated box (KRAB)/KRAB-associated protein 1 (KAP-1)/heterochromatin protein-1 (HP-1) axis alone (non-heritable), or in concert with the DNA methyltransferases DNMT3A and DNMT3L (heritable), mostly hinders prime editors over base editors with the extended portions of prime-editing guide RNAs contributing to this outcome. Indeed, base editors are frequently unhindered or, strikingly, more active at heterochromatin than at euchromatin, an outcome observed neither for prime editors nor nucleases. Critically, the extent and types of byproducts accumulated upon base editing is also contingent upon the epigenetic context of target sequences.

item.title: FASTOP─Fast Editing Toolkit for Top Expression Sites in Yeast.
item.abstract: Budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae is a widely used chassis for producing food- and agriculture-related compounds, but construction of multienzyme pathways often requires repeated genomic integration. We developed FASTOP, a genome-editing toolkit for rapid engineering of eight transcriptionally active genomic hot-spot loci. FASTOP combines selectable markers, extended homology arms, and Cas9/gRNA-assisted integration, and enables PCR-free release of donor cassettes by restriction digestion to reduce sequence errors introduced during amplification. After characterizing the sites, we integrated a five-gene naringenin biosynthetic pathway into the hot spots as a proof of concept. Our results demonstrated that, upon expressing the five essential genes in simple shake-flask culture, naringenin production reached 505.7 mg/L, 6-fold higher than an episomal control expressing the same pathway genes and 4.5-fold higher than the previously reported strain using additional precursor engineering and controlled bioreactor cultivation. FASTOP therefore provides a practical platform for the rapid assembly of multienzyme pathways in yeast for stable heterologous gene expression.

item.title: Advancing Terpenoid Biosynthesis in Saccharomyces cerevisiae: Synthetic Biology Approaches for Efficient Longifolene Production.
item.abstract: The sustainable microbial production of high-value terpenoids like longifolene represents a critical frontier in green manufacturing, yet it is often hindered by systemic metabolic inefficiencies in microbial hosts. To address this, we present a comprehensive systems metabolic engineering framework in Saccharomyces cerevisiae that integrates three complementary modules to overcome the key bottlenecks of enzyme catalysis, cofactor supply, and precursor availability. First, we enhanced the catalytic module by employing the RII dimerization/docking domain-RI anchoring disruptor (RIDD-RIAD) peptide-mediated enzyme assembly and structure-guided Pinus sylvestris longifolene synthase (psTPS) variant screening, `which improved whole-cell longifolene production under the tested conditions. Second, to resolve nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH) cofactor imbalance, we engineered a dual-regeneration system by introducing an exogenous formate dehydrogenase (FDH) and simultaneously amplifying endogenous pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) flux. Third, we reprogrammed central carbon metabolism by integrating the non-oxidative glycolysis (NOG) pathway and deleting the transcriptional repressors DOS2 and YNR063W, and was associated with a larger steady-state cytosolic acetyl-CoA pool, the essential terpenoid precursor. This multi-pronged strategy culminated in a highly optimized strain that achieved a titer of 92.84 mg/L in shake-flask cultures. Critically, the process was successfully scaled to a 5 L bioreactor under fed-batch conditions, yielding 4181.51 mg/L total longifolene at 204 h (3484.79 mg/L extracellular and 696.72 mg/L cell-associated), the highest total titer among the microbial reports identified in Supplementary Table S4. Differences in product recovery and cultivation protocols limit direct process comparisons. Our work demonstrates that coordinated optimization of enzyme assembly, cofactor regeneration, and carbon-flow reprogramming can substantially improve longifolene biosynthesis in S. cerevisiae. This study provides a longifolene-focused case study for modular pathway optimization, while broader application of this strategy to other terpenoids or natural products will require further pathway-specific validation.

item.title: Ca2+ signature gates responsiveness to exogenous auxin in Arabidopsis roots.
item.abstract: Plants must continually balance growth with arrest, especially under stress. Auxin signaling acts as a central regulatory hub in this process, yet the mechanisms that dynamically tune auxin signaling in real time remain unknown. Here, we use the light-gated, Ca2+-permeable Channelrhodopsin 2 variant XXM2.0 to optogenetically impose defined Ca2+ signatures on Arabidopsis root cells. Repetitive light activation triggers cytosolic Ca2+ signals that in turn suppress membrane depolarization and Ca2+ transients triggered by exogenous auxin. Moreover, prolonged optogenetic Ca2+ stimulation affects auxin-responsive transcriptional reprogramming. As phenotypic output, reversible inhibition of root growth by suppressing cell division and elongation is observed. We further identify a candidate CaM7-CNGC14 module that likely mediates Ca2+-dependent gating of responsiveness to exogenous auxin as well as Ca2+-dependent root growth inhibition. Our study thus introduces a synthetic biology approach to decompose calcium-auxin crosstalk in plant cells, and demonstrates that optogenetically imposed cytosolic Ca2+ signals act as dynamic regulators of auxin susceptibility in roots.

item.title: Engineering an α-Amino-ε-Caprolactam Racemase for Efficient d-Phenylalanine Synthesis Using a Coupled Colorimetric Screening Method.
item.abstract: α-Amino-ε-caprolactam racemase (AoACLR) is a key biocatalyst for the synthesis of optically pure d-amino acids, yet its application is constrained by poor activity toward bulky aromatic substrates and limited thermostability. Here, we developed a coupled colorimetric high-throughput screening method and applied directed evolution, structure-guided engineering, and in silico screening to engineer AoACLR. Through combinatorial mutagenesis, we obtained M7 (N17D/L21V/L80T/S211G), which exhibited improved activity, soluble expression, and thermostability. Using l-phenylalaninamide as the substrate, the purified M7 exhibited approximately 1.89-fold higher specific activity toward l-phenylalaninamide than the previously reported L19V/L78T variant, together with 1.63-fold higher residual activity. In a coupled cascade biocatalytic system, M7 produced 14.61 g·L-1d-phenylalanine with 97.78% enantiomeric excess, corresponding to a 2.46-fold increase in d-phenylalanine production. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations suggested that M7 remodeled the substrate access pathway and strengthened the active-site interaction network. This work provides an improved AoACLR variant for efficient d-phenylalanine synthesis.
item.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

item.title: Synergistic Pairwise Residues Identification for Efficient Evolution of Candida antarctica Lipase B for Synthesis of γ- and δ-Lactones.
item.abstract: The lipase enzyme shows great potential for catalyzing the synthesis of valuable food flavor compounds, such as γ- and δ-lactones, but natural lipases are limited by low conversion rates. In this study, we developed a computational-guided strategy named Synergistic Pairwise Residues Evolution for the efficient directed evolution of Candida antarctica lipase B (CalB). This approach identifies synergistic hotspot residues by combining substrate-contact information with evolutionarily coupled functional sectors. E188Q/I189F, the top-performing mutant with 2.75-fold improved activity, achieved over 99.5% conversion within 5 h at 37 °C, compared with only 49% for wild-type CalB in the synthesis of δ-dodecalactone. This study presents an efficient strategy for building functional enzyme toolkits and demonstrates their high catalytic performance in lactone synthesis.

item.title: Resurrecting Robust CYP152 Peroxygenases for Versatile Biocatalysis.
item.abstract: Cytochrome P450 CYP152s are attractive biocatalysts which catalyze decarboxylation and hydroxylation of fatty acids using H2O2 as a co-substrate (peroxygenase activity). Contemporary CYP152s have limited stability and substrate scope. Here we characterized eight reconstructed variants of CYP152 obtained using ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR). The results showed that variants remote from Jeotgalicoccus sp. 8456 (CYP152L1) in the tree used for the ASR tended to catalyze hydroxylation, while nodes closer to CYP152L1 favored decarboxylation; this transition correlates with Q85H substitution and FG-loop insertion alongside other structural features. Three reconstructed variants exhibit high Tm (66°C-76°C), tolerance to solvents, H2O2, extreme pH, and use non-native substrates. CYP152-AncG2 can catalyze one-pot chemoenzymatic C─C bond coupling reactions to synthesize methoxy stilbene and can serve as a template for directed evolution. X-ray structure at 1.83 Å and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations indicate that loop structures, surface salt bridges, and optimized access tunnels in CYP152-AncG2 are key for enabling its superior features. These findings provide insights into the structural and evolutionary features of robust peroxygenase templates for expanding peroxygenase biocatalysis.

item.title: Bone morphogenetic protein 4 meets artificial intelligence: a comprehensive review of AI-driven advances in drug discovery, structural modeling, and clinical translation.
item.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bone Morphogenetic Protein 4 (BMP4), a member of the transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) superfamily, plays pivotal roles in embryonic development, tissue homeostasis, and disease pathogenesis-including cancer, fibrosis, and fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP). The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methodologies over the past 5 years has created unprecedented opportunities for understanding and therapeutically targeting BMP4 biology at multiple scales, from atomic-resolution structure prediction to population-level clinical prognostication.
OBJECTIVE: This review systematically examines the intersection of BMP4 biology and AI across three core domains: (1) AI-driven drug discovery targeting BMP4 signaling pathways, (2) deep learning-based protein structure prediction and computational modeling of BMP4 and its receptor complexes, and (3) clinical AI applications for BMP4-associated diseases.
METHODS: A narrative review with systematic search elements was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, bioRxiv, and arXiv for English-language publications from 2020 to 2026, supplemented by targeted searches via Semantic Scholar. Included studies were categorized as BMP4-specific, BMP receptor/BMP-pathway-targeted, or transferable AI methodology not yet applied to BMP4.
RESULTS: We find that AI has accelerated BMP4-related research along multiple axes, though with important caveats. AlphaFold3 and related tools have generated high-confidence predicted models of BMP4-receptor complex architecture, aspects of which were previously intractable to experimental structure determination; these predictions remain to be fully validated experimentally. ML-guided virtual screening has identified first-in-class BMP pathway (receptor) modulators for FOP, although BMP4-specific small-molecule modulators have not yet been identified computationally. Single-cell transcriptomics combined with machine learning have revealed BMP4's context-dependent roles in glioblastoma cell state transitions and cancer-associated fibroblast biology; and LASSO-Cox regression models incorporating BMP4 expression have shown promising prognostic value in pancreatic adenocarcinoma and gastric cancer, pending prospective validation. Significant gaps persist-most notably the absence of BMP4-specific de novo protein design efforts, the scarcity of large-scale training datasets for BMP4-targeted drug discovery, and the limited integration of multimodal AI approaches in BMP4 clinical research.
CONCLUSION: The convergence of BMP4 biology and AI represents a fertile research Frontier. While foundational tools are now in place, realizing the full translational potential of AI-augmented BMP4 research will require coordinated efforts in data generation, model development, and rigorous experimental and clinical validation. We outline priority directions for the next 5 years (approximately 2026-2031).

item.title: Genetic Engineering Efforts to Generate Chlamydomonas Strains for Large-Scale Biomolecule Production.
item.abstract: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii is an established model microalga. Its easy manipulation, metabolic flexibility and tractable genomes allowed researchers to investigate fundamental processes such as photosynthesis using genetic studies for decades. Chlamydomonas is not naturally rich in lipids or pigments compared to industrially relevant microalgae. However, we highlight how its biotechnological potential relies on advanced genetic and metabolic engineering strategies, now possible due to the availability of extensive toolbox and synthetic biology platforms, which can improve industrial traits and allow to produce a variety of biomolecules of biotechnological interest. We provide examples of biomolecule production (terpenoids and recombinant proteins), and show that productivities (mg/L) are in the same range or could even be higher than those reached in other photosynthetic chassis (e.g., cyanobacteria or mosses). We point out that despite these achievements, the industrial implementation of C. reinhardtii is still lacking. Further technological advancements as well as clear international regulations and social acceptance are fundamental to reach the full potential of this microalga.

item.title: Directed evolution and characterisation of light harvesting complexes with altered spectral properties in purple non-sulfur bacteria.
item.abstract: Purple non-sulfur bacteria (PNSB) are metabolically versatile microorganisms that inhabit diverse environments taking advantage of a remarkably efficient photosynthetic machinery. In this work, we describe the creation of a workflow for experimental studies aiming to compare the light absorption properties of structural variants of the light-harvesting complex 2 (LH2) of PNSB. Through the creation of a library of LH2 variants using site-directed mutagenesis, we engineered proteins with different spectral properties to be expressed in a LH2-defficient mutant of the model PNSB Rhodobacter sphaeroides. We validated this approach by reproducing a previously described mutant with a blue-shift in the B850 absorption peak, in addition to identifying a novel mutant exhibiting a red-shift of this peak. We characterised the fluorescence lifetime of the purified LH2 spectral variants in vitro. Our results suggest that directed evolution approaches can be used to systematically explore the landscape of light absorption in LH2s variants.

item.title: Characterization of a salt-responsive promoter from the moss Physcomitrium patens.
item.abstract: Engineering stress-responsive gene regulation is critical for developing abiotic stress-tolerant plants. Two native Physcomitrium patens promoters was characterized under osmotic and salt stress, identifying Pp3c20_8210 as a salt-inducible promoter in P. patens that could hold a potential in future synthetic biology applications. We also investigated salt-responsive elements in the native promoters of Physcomitrium patens with long-term monitoring of protein expression under high osmotic and saline stress conditions. To evaluate the role of cis-regulatory elements in salt-inducible gene expression, we analyzed shorter engineered versions of Pp3c20_8210, which displayed continuous salt-responsive expression, even after the targeted deletion of key transcription factor binding sites for Homeodomain, MYB, GATA, and Dof transcription factors. Deletion of Homeodomain and GATA transcription factor binding sites reduced Venus reporter expression, suggesting that they are possibly the primary drivers of the Pp3c20_8210 promoter activity in P. patens. No statistically significant effect on promoter responsiveness was detected following the deletion of MYB and Dof transcription factor binding sites under our experimental conditions, possibly due to compensatory mechanisms from other regulatory elements. These findings lay the foundation for future dissection of salt-responsive promoter architecture and can provide valuable tools for synthetic gene regulation in plants.

item.title: Biologically induced spontaneous alginate gelation mediated by extracellular products of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum.
item.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Biological regulation of polysaccharide assembly represents an emerging concept in biofabrication. However, spontaneous gelation of natural polymers driven by bacterial extracellular metabolism remains largely unexplored. This study aimed to characterize a previously unrecognized alginate gelation phenomenon induced by Lactiplantibacillus plantarum without the intentional addition of conventional crosslinking agents.
METHODS: The effects of alginate concentration, bacterial cultivation time, and incubation temperature on gel formation were systematically investigated. The contributions of bacterial cells and cell-free supernatants were evaluated to identify the active fraction responsible for gelation. The role of acidification was examined using defined organic and inorganic acids, and the resulting gel microstructures, secondary Ca2+ crosslinking capability, processability, and bacterial viability during refrigerated storage were assessed.
RESULTS: Reproducible gelation was achieved using 1% (w/v) sodium alginate following 24 h of bacterial cultivation and subsequent incubation at 4 °C. Gel formation depended on bacterial growth, alginate concentration, and low-temperature treatment. Cell-free supernatants retained gelation activity, whereas bacterial cells alone failed to induce gel formation, indicating that extracellular bacterial products mediated the process. Although acidification alone was sufficient to initiate visible gelation, gels formed using defined acids exhibited microstructures distinct from those induced by bacterial extracellular products. Furthermore, the resulting gels remained processable, supported secondary Ca2+ crosslinking, and maintained high bacterial viability during refrigerated storage.
DISCUSSION: These findings demonstrate that extracellular products of L. plantarum can induce alginate gelation under mild conditions without intentionally added conventional crosslinkers. The distinct gel microstructures suggest that bacterial extracellular metabolism may influence gel architecture beyond acidification alone. This biologically induced gelation process provides a foundation for developing bacteria-directed biofabrication strategies, living biomaterials, and biologically engineered hydrogel systems.

item.title: Global health security and smallpox: A strategic review of post-eradication biosafety and preparedness.
item.abstract: The global biosecurity framework faces a potential critical transition driven by synthetic biology advancements and declining population-level immunity. This review evaluates smallpox as a central case study for contemporary pathogen governance and biopolitical preparedness. We analyze the convergence of two primary risks: the technical feasibility of de novo orthopoxvirus synthesis and the expanding immunity gap following the cessation of routine vaccination. The 2022 mpox resurgence is assessed as a sentinel event revealing strategic vulnerabilities in cross-protective immunity. Ultimately, this perspective argues that smallpox reemergence risk is not merely a technological byproduct, but a fundamental global governance crisis. To mitigate these threats, we propose a multidimensional framework integrated with One Health principles and transnational coordination. Maintaining strategic vigilance and institutional memory is presented as a critical political capacity for post-eradication health security.

item.title: Inflammasomes in Atherosclerosis and Atherothrombosis.
item.abstract: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and its thrombotic complications, particularly myocardial infarction and ischemic stroke, remain leading causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Atherosclerosis was historically considered primarily a lipid accumulation disorder; however, it is now well recognized as a chronic inflammatory disesse driven in large part by innate immune signaling. Inflammasomes, particularly NOD-like receptor protein 3 (NLRP3) and absent in melanoma 2 (AIM2), play important role in this process, linking vascular inflammation, plaque progression, and thrombosis through caspase-1 activation, interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β) and IL-18 release, and gasdermin-mediated pyroptosis. In this narrative review we integrate mechanistic and translational evidence defining inflammasome activity across the continuum of atherosclerosis and atherothrombosis. We highlight inflammasome signaling in endothelial cells, macrophages, vascular smooth muscle cells, platelets, neutrophils, and perivascular adipose tissue, and discuss how these pathways contribute to early inflammation, necrotic core expansion, fibrous cap destabilization, and ultimately to acute thrombus formation. Emerging data on AIM2 activation, clonal hematopoiesis, platelet inflammasomes, and cell-free deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) further expand current paradigms beyond macrophage focused models on macrophages. We also review single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, circulating biomarkers, and advanced vascular imaging approaches that may enable the identification of inflammasome-high atherothrombotic phenotypes. Finally, we appraise therapeutic strategies targeting inflammasomes and downstream pathways. These include IL-1β and IL-6 inhibition, colchicine, direct NLRP3 inhibition, and cardiometabolic therapies with indirect effects on inflammasome activity. By examining the role of inflammasomes in linking plaque pathogenesis to thrombosis, this review outlines key translational opportunities and challenges for the precision prevention of atherothrombosis.

item.title: Breeding the unbreedable: bottlenecks and genetic pathways to climate-resilient saffron (Crocus sativus L.).
item.abstract: Cultivated saffron (Crocus sativus L.) is a sterile autotriploid clone (2n = 3x = 24), propagated by corm division for roughly 3,600 years from a single auto-triploidisation event. Sequence-level polymorphism across the global crop is barely 4%, and no F2, recombinant inbred, QTL, or GWAS population has ever been produced, because triploid meiosis forecloses recombination-based breeding outright. This genetic standstill coincides with an accelerating production crisis: Kashmir has lost over 70% of its historical stigma yield, and global stigma yield has fallen by roughly 35% over recent decades. Methylation polymorphism across the World Saffron and Crocus Collection is eight-fold higher than sequence polymorphism, making epigenetic divergence the only substantial non-mutagenic source of heritable variation currently accessible. Heat, drought, cold, and Fusarium-driven disease converge on the florigen activation complex and the apocarotenoid pathway, defining a compact target set led by CsatSVP2, CsCCD2, and a defined NBS-LRR resistance-gene catalogue. Against the genomic infrastructure now available, including a fully phased 8.42 Gb triploid assembly, we evaluate the strategies open to this crop: epigenomic selection, clean-stock reform, induced mutagenesis, soma-clonal selection, wild-relative pre-breeding, and CRISPR/base/prime editing. Improvement is no longer limited mainly by a shortage of molecular targets or tools, but by a small number of translational bottlenecks, foremost the absence of any published whole-plant regeneration pipeline for edited tissue. We rank these bottlenecks by dependency and set out our own view of research priorities for the next five to fifteen years.

cards.why_it_matters: 政府云环境开放专用网络安全模型，反映 AI 在受监管场景的合规部署路径；合成生物学研究者可关注其生物安全与双用途审查机制。

item.title: Big Tech claims voters’ AI backlash is “anti-Trump” not “anti-tech”
item.abstract: Tech industry in denial as US overwhelmingly votes to restrict AI, data centers.

cards.score_reason: AI政治舆论，弱相关
cards.title_cn: 科技巨头称选民对AI的反弹是“反特朗普”而非“反科技”
cards.one_liner: 美国选民压倒性投票限制AI与数据中心，科技巨头却将其解读为“反特朗普”情绪。
key_findings: 美国选民以压倒性票数通过限制AI和数据中心的措施。
科技行业否认这是对技术本身的反对，归因于政治情绪。
行业与公众在AI治理上的认知分歧正在扩大。
cards.why_it_matters: 美国AI监管风向与公众态度直接影响合成生物学AI工具的合规环境与产业政策，值得关注政策风险。

cards.one_liner: Cruz 与 Trump 似无意填补 FCC 民主党空缺席位，欲抢先扩增共和党委员。
key_findings: Cruz 计划在民主党接管参议院前，为 FCC 增补共和党委员。
Cruz 与 Trump 似无计划填补 FCC 的民主党空缺席位。
cards.why_it_matters: FCC 委员党派构成将影响美国频谱分配、通信与生物技术相关无线监管走向，对在美布局的合成生物学团队有间接影响。

item.title: California fights "preposterous" Trump admin demand to scrap state broadband laws
item.abstract: State tries to obtain broadband funds despite rejecting Trump admin condition.

cards.score_reason: 宽带政策纠纷，弱相关
cards.title_cn: 加州拒绝特朗普政府废除州宽带法规的要求，称其“荒谬”
cards.one_liner: 加州为争取宽带资金，拒绝特朗普政府要求废除州宽带法规的条件。
key_findings: 加州拒绝接受特朗普政府以废除州宽带法规为条件的宽带资金。
加州称该要求“荒谬”，并试图在拒绝条件的同时仍获得资金。
cards.why_it_matters: 该新闻涉及美国宽带政策与联邦资金分配，与合成生物学研究方向无直接关联，仅作一般产业政策背景了解。
